claim: Last-wolf chanteuse should speak only from facts the Game Master announced, 'such as confirmed shots, announced roleblocks, and revealed roles'.
rule: Roleblocks are never announced; the morning report covers only attacks, saves, deaths, roles and wills. A roleblock a player mentions is their own claim.

claim: The information landscape includes 'an announced roleblock' and a sigil placement with no effect as public facts the town builds a case on.
rule: Roleblocks and sigil results are private to the player (told 'You were roleblocked' / told the sigil had no effect); the Game Master announces neither.

claim: When a player cites watch-type information while the Sentinel is 'dead and unrevealed', argue that they are the Necromancer working through the dead Sentinel's body.
rule: A Necromancer can only use a dead player whose role was announced; a body whose role was hidden cannot be used. An unrevealed Sentinel body is not available to it.

claim: The Investigator's Night 1 check was roleblocked, so 'no charge was spent'.
rule: The rules say a blocked action is not carried out and makes no visit, but do not say whether the check is spent; the claim is unsupported.

claim: An attack announced as made through a body, 'or a hidden-role death', shows that a Necromancer is alive.
rule: A reanimated-attack announcement shows a Necromancer; a hidden-role death alone does not, since an Illusionist hides the role of the wolves' victim.

claim: With four alive, removing the lone killer while a wolf survives 'leaves the wolf at parity'.
rule: Wolves win only when they equal or outnumber everyone else alive; one wolf against two others (after the killer is voted out) is not parity.

claim: An immune shot result is strong evidence of a Serial Killer, and a Fortune Teller self-bet is the one alternative to rule out.
rule: The Necromancer also cannot be killed on the first night, so an immune result on night 1 also fits it; the rules name more than one alternative.

claim: A shot returning 'immune' is something 'only a Serial Killer or a Fortune Teller self-bet would produce', so name that player as the Serial Killer.
rule: The Necromancer is also unkillable on the first night, so an immune shot then fits it too.

claim: A Chanteuse block means no sigil is placed and none is spent.
rule: The rules say a blocked action is not carried out but do not say whether the sigil is spent; they only say a sigil is spent when placed.

claim: A no-effect result 'means the target did not attack'.
rule: No effect is also what an attacker protected by night immunity (e.g. the Serial Killer) looks like, so it does not show the target did not attack.

claim: Prefer a suspected lone killer, who attacks every night, over a wolf as the sigil target.
rule: The sigil's strike is an attack that night immunity stops; a Serial Killer cannot be killed at night, and a Necromancer does not attack every night.

claim: A placed sigil 'strikes any wolf carrier or killer who attacks the target'.
rule: A sigil strikes the player it was placed on if that player attacks anyone that night; it does not strike others who attack that player.

claim: Claiming no ability 'fits only a villager or the killer'.
rule: There is no plain villager role; the world is closed and every dealt role has a listed ability or win condition.
